investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-22T00:27:03Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first network call to the swarm gateway, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB endpoint that backs POST /api/agents → /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api runtime at the time of the eval run. This is an infrastructure-layer failure upstream of the eval runner: the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never received a successful response, so the probe terminated with a 502 before any evidence could be written. The failure is localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

possibleCauses: Primary: The swarm gateway ELB (us-east-2) was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api to receive a 502 when forwarding POST /api/agents to /v1/agents.

Secondary: A network routing or security-group change between the production-api and the swarm ELB blocked outbound connectivity to the ELB endpoint, resulting in a connection error surfaced as 502 bad_gateway.
Tertiary: The swarm service itself (behind the ELB) was restarting, overloaded, or had crashed, causing the ELB to return 502 with no healthy backends.

Lower probability: A transient DNS or TLS resolution failure for the ELB hostname caused the request to fail before reaching any backend, producing the 'error sending request' message seen in failed-check.message.
